post.description:
Provision the account and its workspace organization (IDR-016).

The registrant becomes `organization_admin` of a fresh workspace, and the
consent receipts for every active account-level statement are recorded
atomically with the account. Registration does not log in — call
`POST /auth/login` next.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the quota resets. Sent with `429`.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description:
Open a server-side session and set the `__Host-session` cookie.

Unknown email, disabled account, and wrong password all answer the same
`401`. A locked account answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the quota resets. Sent with `429`.

get.description: The current user, organization, and server-side expiry horizon.

post.description: Revoke the session server-side and clear the cookie.

Verify the current password, re-encrypt, and rotate every session.

Sessions on other devices are revoked; this one is replaced and the new
cookie is set on the response (session regeneration on privilege change).

Launch a domain or file scan.

Returns `202` with the job resource. An unauthenticated launch also returns the
one-time token needed to claim the scan after registering.

The application performs the launch in a fixed order: allocate the job
identifier, record any required declarations against it, evaluate the gates,
create job and task state in one transaction, enqueue only once that state is
durable, then respond. Gates — authorization, verification, current MFA
assurance, rate, and cooldown — are evaluated from the request context and the
selected tests. None of them is a field the caller sends.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the quota resets. Sent with `429`.

requestBody.description:
The request schema is selected by media type, and within JSON by access state.

- `application/json` + authenticated caller → `AssetScanLaunch` (`asset_id`, an Asset in the caller's organization).
- `application/json` + anonymous caller → `GuestScanLaunch` (`target`, a canonical domain).
- `multipart/form-data` → `FileScanLaunch` (one `file` part, no target).

Supplying the field belonging to the other access state returns `422`. No schema contains an `asset_id | target | file` union, and no other media type is accepted.

200.description:
Advisory progress events until the job reaches a terminal state. The SSE `event:` line selects the payload:

- `task` → `ScanTaskEvent`, one task changed state
- `job` → `ScanJobEvent`, the job changed state
- `heartbeat` → `ScanHeartbeatEvent`, sent on an interval
- `end` → `ScanEndEvent`, terminal state reached, no further events

Database state is authoritative. Refetch the snapshot after a reconnect or whenever an applied event leaves the client uncertain.

post.description:
Record durable cancellation intent.

Scan history is preserved: canceling is not deletion, and `DELETE` is never
used to stop execution. Workers check the intent before starting a task and at
safe interruption points; a canceled task cannot later produce an accepted
successful result.

Attach a guest scan to the authenticated caller's organization.

One atomic compare-and-set: the job must be an unclaimed guest job whose stored
hash matches the supplied token and whose retention has not lapsed. Success
records the claiming user and organization and discards the stored hash, so the
token cannot be spent twice. For a file scan it also restores organization
scoping on the upload metadata.

Every failure answers `404` — wrong token, already claimed, and lapsed are
indistinguishable from outside. Anything more specific would let a caller
holding no token confirm that a scan exists and learn its state.

Move `purge_at` further out and record an audit event.

No request body: the interval is policy, not contract.
Read the new deadline from the response.

post.description:
Issue a challenge at the requested coverage.

Requires current MFA assurance, read from the OIDC token rather than from any
stored flag — proving control of a domain is what later authorizes scanning it.

On an already-verified asset the response carries both the standing proof and
the new challenge, so coverage in force is never withdrawn while ownership is
re-proven.

Resolve the challenge record and update the state.

Always sets `last_recheck_at`, so a user who presses this while DNS is still
propagating can see that it ran. Propagation takes anywhere from minutes to
two days, which makes "not found yet" the common outcome rather than an
exceptional one.

A check that ran and found nothing is a result, not a fault: the response is
`200` with the state still `pending` and a `failure_code` saying why.

Issue a fresh token and expiry for a stalled challenge.

Answers `409` when the asset is already verified. Regeneration exists for a
challenge that expired or whose token was lost, and a verified asset has
neither — replacing its token would discard a working proof and make the user
edit DNS again to get back where they started.

To re-prove ownership, or to widen the scope, start a new challenge with
`POST .../verification`. The existing `verified_scope` holds until that
challenge succeeds, so nothing depending on the current proof breaks meanwhile.

post.description:
Issue an invitation and email the link.

Answers `409` when a live invitation already exists for the same address. There
is no resend: revoke the outstanding one and issue another, so every link ever
sent has its own auditable row.

delete.description:
Invalidate the outstanding link.

The row survives with `revoked_at` set, which is why this returns the invitation
rather than `204` — revocation changes state, it does not erase it.

post.description:
Join the organization.

Atomic, and gated on three things at once: the token is live, the caller's
verified email matches the invited address, and the caller does not already
belong to another organization. Failing any of them changes nothing.

Rejects any statement that requires a context: a per-launch declaration is bound

get.description:
Audit entries in chain order.

Ordered by (`chain_id`, `sequence_number`) rather than by time, because that
pair is what defines the hash chain — reading in timestamp order would not let
a verifier follow `previous_hash` from one entry to the next.

Encrypted payloads are returned as ciphertext. Decryption is a separate operator
procedure and is not exposed by v4.0.

DnsRecordType.title: DnsRecordType
DnsRecordType.description:
DNS record a verification challenge is published as.

TXT is the only v4.0 method.

status.description: `verified` whenever a proof exists, whatever the challenge is doing. `pending` while an unanswered challenge is still answerable. `expired` once it is no longer answerable and no proof exists.

verified_scope.description: Coverage actually proven, null until a challenge first succeeds. Requesting a wider scope does not widen this until that challenge succeeds, so an existing proof is never silently upgraded.

verified_at.title: Verified At
verified_at.description: When the proof was recorded. Non-null exactly when `verified_scope` is.

challenge.description: The challenge currently running, or null when none is. It appears alongside `verified_scope` while an already-verified domain re-proves ownership or widens its coverage.

DomainVerification.title: DomainVerification
DomainVerification.description:
Current ownership state of one domain: the proof, plus any challenge running against it.

The proof and the challenge are independent.
A domain that is already verified keeps `verified_scope` while a new challenge runs, so re-proving ownership or widening coverage never withdraws coverage that is already proven.

Only the current state lives here.
Attempts and transitions are recorded in the audit log.

claim_token.description: The one-time token returned by the unauthenticated launch.

ScanClaimRequest.title: ScanClaimRequest
ScanClaimRequest.description:
Claims a guest scan for the authenticated caller's organization.

The token travels in the body rather than a header: it authorizes one operation
on one resource, not the caller, and `Authorization` already carries the session
that identifies who is claiming.

ScanClassification.title: ScanClassification
ScanClassification.description:
Intrusiveness of one executable test, copied onto the task at creation.

`not_applicable` is used only by File tests.

ScanGrade.title: ScanGrade
ScanGrade.description: Letter grade. Produced by the scan modules.

organization_id.title: Organization Id
organization_id.description: Owning organization, and the row-level-security key. Null for a guest job until it is claimed. Tasks, results, and findings inherit it, so it is not repeated on those resources.

source.description: Derived server-side from the request context, never supplied by the caller. It selects which gates apply.

triggered_by_user_id.title: Triggered By User Id
triggered_by_user_id.description: Attribution only. Becomes null if the user is erased.

target_domain.title: Target Domain
target_domain.description: Canonical domain that is not an Asset row. Populated only by an unauthenticated launch; a guest target never becomes an Asset.

file_upload_id.title: File Upload Id
file_upload_id.description: The upload created by an accepted multipart launch. At most one per job.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: What the launch asked for. Compare against the tasks to see what ran: a requested module whose task was blocked or skipped produced nothing.

status_reason.title: Status Reason
status_reason.description: Stable namespaced reason code for a job-wide exceptional or terminal outcome. A job timeout sets the job-timeout reason and resolves to `partial` when usable results exist, otherwise `failed`.

purge_at.title: Purge At
purge_at.description:
Read-only final hard-deletion timestamp, not the start of a grace period. Null until terminal completion, then `finished_at` plus twelve months plus thirty days by default, with thirty days' notice.

An unclaimed guest job is the exception: it carries a deadline from creation, because ownerless data has nobody to notify and no reason to be kept. A successful claim recomputes this under the normal rule, and notice begins to apply only from that point. Purging at the deadline does not wait for the job to finish; unfinished work is terminated.

ScanJob.title: ScanJob
ScanJob.description:
One submitted scan request.

Exactly one of `asset_id`, `target_domain`, and `file_upload_id` is set, chosen
by the request context rather than by the caller: an authenticated JSON launch
populates `asset_id`, an unauthenticated JSON launch populates `target_domain`,
and a multipart launch populates `file_upload_id`.

organization_id.description: Owning organization, and the row-level-security key. Null for a guest job until it is claimed. Tasks, results, and findings inherit it, so it is not repeated on those resources.

claim_token.title: Claim Token
claim_token.description: One-time token that claims this scan for an organization once the guest registers. Present only on the response to an unauthenticated launch, and readable only here — the server keeps a hash, so a lost token cannot be recovered and the scan stays unclaimable.

ScanJobAccepted.title: ScanJobAccepted
ScanJobAccepted.description:
The `202` body of a launch.

Identical to a ScanJob except that an unauthenticated launch also returns the
one-time token needed to claim the scan after registering.

organization_id.title: Organization Id
organization_id.description: Owning organization, and the row-level-security key. Null for a guest job until it is claimed. Tasks, results, and findings inherit it, so it is not repeated on those resources.

triggered_by_user_id.description: Attribution only. Becomes null if the user is erased.

file_upload_id.description: The upload created by an accepted multipart launch. At most one per job.

ScanJobDetail.title: ScanJobDetail
ScanJobDetail.description:
A job together with its task snapshot.

This is the snapshot a live-progress client fetches before subscribing, and
refetches after a reconnect. Results are a separate call because they are large.

ScanJobStatus.title: ScanJobStatus
ScanJobStatus.description: Job lifecycle. `partial` means usable results exist alongside failures.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: Version of the result payload written by this test. Text, not a number: the registry versions each test's result schema independently.

raw_output.title: Raw Output
raw_output.description: Full test output. Shape owned by the executable-test registry.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Condensed verdicts for display. Non-graded tests carry their per-step verdicts here. Shape owned by the executable-test registry.

grade.description: Letter grade. Present only for `email.mailvalidator`, `web.headers`, and `web.tls`. No cross-module composite score exists.

severity_counts.description: Findings by severity. Used by non-graded tests.

trend.description: Movement against the previous result for this test, tracking `grade` where the test is graded and total findings where it is not. Null on the first result for a test, or once the predecessor has been purged.

ScanResult.title: ScanResult
ScanResult.description: The output of one completed ScanTask. At most one per task.

ScanSource.title: ScanSource
ScanSource.description:
What requested a scan job.

Derived from the request context, never supplied by the caller.

parent_task_id.title: Parent Task Id
parent_task_id.description: Discovery and fan-out lineage. A subdomain found by `web.subdomain_enumeration` becomes a child task of the discovering one.

test_key.title: Test Key
test_key.description: Stable identifier of the executable test. v4.0 catalog: `email.mailvalidator`, `web.headers`, `web.tls`, `web.subdomain_enumeration`, `file.hashlookup`, `file.pandora`, `file.metadata`, `file.mime_check`, `pqc.quantumvalidator`, `dnssec.chainvalidator`. The vocabulary is code-owned and extends without a schema change.

test_version.title: Test Version
test_version.description: Version of the test definition, copied at task creation.

target_domain.title: Target Domain
target_domain.description: Set for a guest target or a discovered subdomain with no Asset row.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: Resolved per-test configuration. Shape owned by the test registry.

status_reason.title: Status Reason
status_reason.description: Stable namespaced reason code for a failed, skipped, blocked, or canceled outcome. Always present when the status is `blocked`. A task timeout appears as `failed` plus the task-timeout reason: timeout is a reason, never a status. Labels and localization are code-owned.

cancellation_requested_at.title: Cancellation Requested At
cancellation_requested_at.description: Durable cancellation intent. Workers check it before starting and at safe interruption points; a canceled task cannot later produce an accepted successful result.

ScanTask.title: ScanTask
ScanTask.description:
One executable test run against one domain or one uploaded file.

Exactly one of `target_asset_id`, `target_domain`, and `file_upload_id` is set.
`id` doubles as the queue task identifier and as the public `task_id` carried by
live-progress events.

ScanTaskStatus.title: ScanTaskStatus
ScanTaskStatus.description:
Task lifecycle.

`blocked` always carries a `status_reason` explaining why,
so the UI can tell the user what stopped a check.

created_by_user_id.title: Created By User Id
created_by_user_id.description: Attribution only. The schedule is organization-owned.

recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule
recurrence_rule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE, without the `RRULE:` prefix, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;BYHOUR=2;BYMINUTE=0`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone the rule is evaluated in, e.g. `Europe/Luxembourg`. Stored separately from the rule so local run times survive daylight-saving changes.

next_run_at.title: Next Run At
next_run_at.description: Next fire time. Null while disabled or once the rule is exhausted.

Schedule.title: Schedule
Schedule.description: A recurring scan of one asset.

recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule
recurrence_rule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE, without the `RRULE:` prefix, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;BYHOUR=2;BYMINUTE=0`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone the rule is evaluated in, e.g. `Europe/Luxembourg`. Stored separately from the rule so local run times survive daylight-saving changes.

ScheduleCreate.title: ScheduleCreate
ScheduleCreate.description:
Create a recurring scan.

The asset must already be eligible under the verification rules. Eligibility is
rechecked at every execution rather than trusted from creation time, so a
verification that lapses stops producing scans instead of quietly continuing.

recurrence_rule.title: Recurrence Rule
recurrence_rule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE, without the `RRULE:` prefix, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;BYHOUR=2;BYMINUTE=0`.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone the rule is evaluated in, e.g. `Europe/Luxembourg`. Stored separately from the rule so local run times survive daylight-saving changes.

ScheduleUpdate.title: ScheduleUpdate
ScheduleUpdate.description:
Partial update. Omitted fields are left alone.

`asset_id` is absent: repointing a schedule at another asset would attribute one
asset's recurring history to a different one.

SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo
SessionInfo.description:
The authenticated session and its server-side expiry horizon.

`idle_expires_at` moves with activity; `absolute_expires_at` never does.
Whichever passes first ends the session (Non-functional v0.11).

SeverityCounts.title: SeverityCounts
SeverityCounts.description:
Findings counted by severity band.

Stored as untyped JSONB in `scan_result.severity_counts`, but the key set is fully determined by `finding_severity`, so the contract types it.
Non-graded tests summarize outcomes through these counts instead of a letter grade; graded tests carry both.

required_context_type.title: Required Context Type
required_context_type.description: Null for an account-level statement. `scan_job` for a per-launch one, whose response must be bound to the launch it belongs to.

content_hash.title: Content Hash
content_hash.description: Hash of the exact text, so a receipt can prove what was shown.

Statement.title: Statement
Statement.description:
One currently active versioned statement.

Active means `effective_at` has passed and the statement is not retired.

StatementResponseKind.title: StatementResponseKind
StatementResponseKind.description: Acceptance and attestation share a receipt shape but are distinct acts.

context_id.title: Context Id
context_id.description: The bound resource — a ScanJob for a per-launch response.

StatementResponseReceipt.title: StatementResponseReceipt
StatementResponseReceipt.description:
Proof that a statement was answered.

Immutable: a correction is a new statement version and a new response, never an
edit. Actor evidence is deliberately absent from this representation.

version.title: Version
version.description: Exact version answered, as returned by `GET /statements`.

StatementResponseSubmission.title: StatementResponseSubmission
StatementResponseSubmission.description:
A client's answer to one statement, identified by key and version.

The version is explicit, so the receipt records the exact text that was shown,
not whichever version happened to be current.

TechnicalReportView.title: TechnicalReportView
TechnicalReportView.description: Depth of a technical report. Meaningful only when the evidence tier is technical.

TrendDirection.title: TrendDirection
TrendDirection.description: Movement of a score against the previous comparable measurement.

requested_scope.description: Coverage this challenge proves if it succeeds.

record_type.description: Type of DNS record to create.

record_name.title: Record Name
record_name.description: Name of the DNS record to create. Computed by the server from the asset's domain and a deployment-configured vendor prefix. Display the returned value; do not rebuild it.

verification_token.title: Verification Token
verification_token.description: Complete value of the record, pasted verbatim. The client does not wrap, prefix, or encode it.

token_expires_at.title: Token Expires At
token_expires_at.description: When the challenge stops being answerable. Seven days from issue by default. Reaching it retires the challenge; a proof already recorded is unaffected.

last_recheck_at.title: Last Recheck At
last_recheck_at.description: When the record was last looked for, whatever triggered the lookup — a user pressing verify, or the recheck that runs before an intrusive task is queued. Null until the first check. Pair it with `failure_code` to show why the last attempt did not succeed.

failure_code.title: Failure Code
failure_code.description: Stable namespaced reason the last check did not succeed.

VerificationChallenge.title: VerificationChallenge
VerificationChallenge.description:
A DNS record to publish to prove control of the domain.

Present while a challenge is answerable, and while its last check is being shown.
Absent once the challenge has produced its proof and absent on a domain with no challenge running.

requested_scope.description: `exact` covers this domain alone. `zone` covers it and everything beneath it, evaluated by DNS-label ancestry rather than string suffix, so `evil-example.lu` is never treated as part of `example.lu`.

VerificationCreate.title: VerificationCreate
VerificationCreate.description: Start a domain-ownership challenge at a chosen coverage.

VerificationScope.title: VerificationScope
VerificationScope.description: Verification coverage. Zone coverage is evaluated by DNS-label ancestry.

VerificationStatus.title: VerificationStatus
VerificationStatus.description: Current state of a domain-ownership challenge.

AssetScanLaunch.description:
Authenticated domain launch.

Selected by `application/json` plus an authenticated caller.

modules.description: One or more distinct modules to run against the target.
modules.title: Modules

module_configuration.description: Per-module launch options. Each module defines its own option shape; the web module's subdomain-discovery option is one example.
module_configuration.title: Module Configuration

statement_responses.description: Answers to the statements this launch requires, each identified by key and version. Recorded as immutable receipts bound to the job before any gate is evaluated. Empty in practice for v4.0: a declaration is required only by an intrusive test, and the v4.0 catalog classifies none. A boolean `attestation` flag is not a substitute and is not part of this contract.
statement_responses.title: Statement Responses

asset_id.description: An Asset belonging to the caller's organization.
asset_id.title: Asset Id

AssetScanLaunch.title: AssetScanLaunch

FileScanLaunch.description:
File launch. Selected by `multipart/form-data`.

Carries no target field and no `modules` field.
The resulting job is always the File module.

file.description: The file to analyze. Maximum 50 MB by default. The MIME type is detected from the raw bytes; the declared `Content-Type` and the filename extension are not trusted.
file.title: File

FileScanLaunch.title: FileScanLaunch

GuestScanLaunch.description:
Unauthenticated domain launch.

Selected by `application/json` plus an anonymous caller.

Free target text exists in this context and nowhere else. The domain is stored
on the job and never becomes an Asset row. Guest launches run non-intrusive
tests only, which in v4.0 is every domain test.

modules.description: One or more distinct modules to run against the target.
modules.title: Modules

module_configuration.description: Per-module launch options. Each module defines its own option shape; the web module's subdomain-discovery option is one example.
module_configuration.title: Module Configuration

statement_responses.description: Answers to the statements this launch requires, each identified by key and version. Recorded as immutable receipts bound to the job before any gate is evaluated. Empty in practice for v4.0: a declaration is required only by an intrusive test, and the v4.0 catalog classifies none. A boolean `attestation` flag is not a substitute and is not part of this contract.
statement_responses.title: Statement Responses

target.description: Domain to scan. Unicode or ASCII input is accepted and canonicalized to lowercase IDNA (A-label) form without a trailing dot.
target.title: Target

GuestScanLaunch.title: GuestScanLaunch

ScanEndEvent.description: SSE `end`: the job reached a terminal state and no further events follow.
ScanEndEvent.title: ScanEndEvent

ScanHeartbeatEvent.description:
SSE `heartbeat`: the stream is alive.

Sent on an interval so a client can tell a running scan from a dropped
connection, and show when it last heard anything.
ScanHeartbeatEvent.title: ScanHeartbeatEvent

SessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie set by `POST /auth/login`. HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; the session record and its idle/absolute timeouts are enforced server-side.
SessionCookie.name: __Host-session

OpenIdConnect.description: OpenID Connect token issued by the platform identity provider. Some operations additionally require current MFA assurance, read from the token at request time.

ApiKey.description: Platform API key: `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Scopes are `read_only` and `full_scan`. A scan launched with a key is recorded with `source = api`. Creating or revoking a key requires an OpenID Connect token with current MFA assurance.
ApiKey.name: Authorization
